title: Return to Sender
priority: Narrative clarity, specific word choice and character agency; retain the existing sound approach.
logline: A courier tries to cancel a delivery that has already been marked complete. The lift carries her to the person who ordered it.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: The label says delivered. She hasn't handed it to anyone.

phrases.text: She hasn't handed it to anyone.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: She's taking it to the lobby.

narration.speaker: courier
narration.text: Cancel it. I'm taking it back.

editorial_changes: State the visible contradiction immediately, without inventing a signature, name or unseen event.
Replace commentary about speed with a question that motivates the following parcel insert.
Replace the repeated holding-the-parcel observation with a concrete cancellation attempt.
Call dispatch once, then let the unanswered request and failed control press escalate.
Name the missed destination rather than merely reading the display's zero.
Make the refusal explicit so Keep it directly answers her choice.
Retain the concise final reversal and the speech-free opening-door reveal.
